Alternatively, send the duly filled application with relevant documents via email to [email protected] . Ensure the application reaches the office on or before 14 October 2026 at 5:00 PM.

faq.question: Q1. What is Jogulamba Gadwal District Aspirational Block Fellow Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is a recruitment notification released by the Office of the District Collector, Jogulamba Gadwal, to hire 1 Aspirational Block Fellow under the Aspirational Block Programme, NITI Aayog.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available under this notification?
faq.answer: There is a total of 1 vacancy available for the Aspirational Block Fellow post.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: The last date to submit the application is 14 October 2026 up to 5:00 PM.

faq.question: Q4. What is the educational qualification required?
faq.answer: Candidates must possess a Post Graduate with First Class in any discipline from a reputed institution.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for this recruitment?
faq.answer: The minimum age is 23 years and the maximum age is 38 years as on 01.01.2026, with relaxations as per applicable Government rules.

faq.question: Q6. Is there any application fee?
faq.answer: The notification does not mention any application fee.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply for this post?
faq.answer: Candidates can apply through the prescribed offline process by submitting a sealed envelope via Registered Post/Speed Post or by emailing the application to [email protected].

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process?
faq.answer: The selection process comprises a writing skill test, a brief PowerPoint presentation, an explanation/data analysis test, a computer/IT skill and personality test, and an interview/viva voce.

faq.question: Q9. What is the monthly salary?
faq.answer: The selected candidate will receive a monthly stipend of Rs. 55,000/-, along with travel allowance up to Rs. 5,000/- per month.

faq.question: Q10. Is this a permanent government job?
faq.answer: No, the engagement is purely temporary in nature and does not confer any right for regular appointment.
